text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts in prod-ingress (region-eu). Threshold breached: 5xx rate 18% over last 2m, p99 latency 4.2s. Paging on-call (raj). :rotating_light:

raj: I’m on it. seeing repeated gateway 502/504s from the ingress fronting the scheduler. Can folks avoid pushing deploys to prod for next 20m?

emma: on standby. can you paste the initial query/alert and the affected customer list?

incident-bot: Alert details -> rule: prod.ingress.gateway.errors > 10% for 60s. Top error: 502 gateway timeout; affected routes: /v1/generate (high), /v1/chat (medium). Top customers by error volume: customer-alpha, beta-sa, internal-canary.

raj: quick triage note: scheduler batch queue length jumped from ~200 to ~2.5k in 3m. head-of-line blocking observed on batcher-nodes eu-*-gpu. Likely backlog causing token generation timeouts which bubble up as gateway 504s.

tom: logs show continuous KV fetch latency spikes around same time; kvcache hitrate dropped and prefetch tasks backing up. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] batcher-03 WARN kvprefetch: request_queue_size=1248, prefetch_latency_ms=3120, retry=1
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] gateway-02 ERROR upstream_timeout id=0x9f234
```

lucy: can we confirm whether this is a demand spike vs a regression? any deploys in last 30m?

maria: no prod deploys in last 45m. metric trends show a client-side surge from customer-alpha sending long sequences. Looks like a few heavy sessions pushing long context lengths (100k tokens combined) -> big batches forming.

raj: action plan (initial):
- 1) Route heavy clients to the slower, high-memory pool (eu-large) to reduce pressure on default scheduler. (temporary routing rule)
- 2) Scale batcher-nodes + increase batch processing parallelism by +30% (if infra quota allows).
- 3) Enable aggressive eviction for low-priority queues and reduce max batch size config to force faster flush.
- 4) If routing/scale not enough, enable fallback to smaller model-variant for affected routes to keep latency SLOs.

emma: I’ll do step 1 and 3. tom, can you check kvcache and redis latency? if kvcache prefetch is failing we need to clear stuck prefetch tasks.

tom: on it. running: `redis-cli -h kv-prefetch-eu INFO` and `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=batcher -o wide`. Also checking scheduler queue distribution.

lucy: tagging @support to prep incident page and list impacted customers + expected ETA for next update.

support-bot: Incident page created: https://status.internal/redwood/incident/1719600000. Notified CSMs for customer-alpha, beta-sa.

raj: rolling the temporary routing rule now: `redwood route add --match customer:customer-alpha --to eu-large --ttl 15m --note "mitigate hol blocking"`

emma: done. also lowered max_batch_size from 64->32 for fronting scheduler (hotfix) via: `config apply scheduler.front.max_batch_size=32 --rollout immediate`

tom: redis INFO shows `used_memory_peak` spike and `blocked_clients` ~ 8. kvcache prefetch workers at 95% utilization; clearing stuck tasks: `kubectl exec -n infra redis-0 -- redis-cli CLIENT KILL TYPE normal` (careful). I’m restarting the prefetch controller pod to force requeue.

raj: monitoring queue length now. metric update: queue length dropping from 2.5k -> 700 over 90s. 5xx rate dropping to 6%. p95 latency down to 1.8s.

maria: customer-alpha traffic dropped 80% after routing; beta-sa still noisy (some retries). Support: customer-alpha reported degraded service earlier, they now see improvement.

lucy: quick ask — do we need to page infra for additional GPU capacity? capacity pool eu-large has 2 spare nodes; can we spin them?

emma: I can scale up two nodes from dedicated-pool-eu: `infra scale pool dedicated-pool-eu +2` — doing it now, should be up in ~3m.

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler triggered an error when trying to launch new instances: `quota_exceeded`. Need manual approval.

raj: ack. paging infra-ops (maria) for quota lift — @maria can you approve spot/ondemand boost?

maria: approving now, contacting cloud-ops. ETA 4m for quota lift and instance bootstrap.

tom: prefetch controller restarted. kvcache hitrate recovering. scheduler batch flush improved. I see fewer evictions and less per-batch token count.

raj: 5xx rate now 2.1%, p99 latency 1.1s. Gateway timeouts down to baseline. We should keep routing and smaller batch size until traffic normalizes.

lucy: coordinating on-call handoff: I’ll take over for next 20m to monitor (lucy -> monitoring lead). @raj handoff to @lucy — please include any outstanding items.

raj: Handoff: issue was HOL blocking due to long-context heavy sessions from customer-alpha followed by KV prefetch saturation. Actions done: temp route to eu-large (15m), reduced max_batch_size, restarted kvcache prefetch controller, scaled +2 nodes (pending quota), eviction policy tightened. Monitoring to watch: queue_length, kv_prefetch_latency, 5xx_rate. No code change deployed. I’m available if it flares.

lucy: taking it. I’ll keep the incident page updated and send a brief customer impact note once stability confirmed for 15m.

support-bot: Customer update draft: "We observed elevated error rates impacting customers X and Y due to scheduler queue buildup causing timeouts. We applied routing and batch size mitigations and are monitoring — service quality returning to normal. Will follow up with incident report." Approve to send?

maria: approve. add note about no data leak, no model regressions.

emma: small follow-up: add a runbook action item — add alert to detect persistent high per-session token rates to proactively route heavy sessions.

raj: agreed. adding task to infra backlog: "session-length routing rule + per-session token threshold alert".

lucy: final update: 30m since mitigation, 5xx steady at 0.9%, queue length stable ~120. Closing paging for now. Will open postmortem doc template and assign owners for root cause deep-dive. Thanks team. :tada:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: automated monitoring will keep extra retention for 48h.

lucy: postmortem owners: raj (root cause), tom (kvcache), emma (routing/ops), maria (capacity/quota). I’ll create the postmortem doc and link here.
